signal_rationale.delta: The report revisits the historical claim that war is a recurring engine of Western development, connecting US wartime R&D, West German reconstruction and contemporary European defence procurement through the mechanisms of industrial conversion.
signal_rationale.evidence: Gross and Sampat (AER 2023) identify persistent OSRD innovation-cluster effects; Field (2022) documents wartime manufacturing productivity losses; US Economic Report 1991 and IMF historical analysis document West German recovery; BMW and USHMM histories document forced labour and postwar dismantling; ECB and IMF 2026 studies assess defence-spending multipliers and productivity channels.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Public procurement and R&D → engineering, supplier and production capabilities → civilian diffusion and export competitiveness; destruction, imports and fragmented demand can interrupt this chain.
signal_rationale.transmission: Military demand and research funding → capital formation, standards and technical knowledge → surviving industrial capacity → postwar conversion, trade and productivity; fiscal burdens and physical destruction operate in the opposite direction.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The development-conversion thesis would weaken if defence R&D and domestic equipment procurement repeatedly failed to produce measurable supplier capability, civilian diffusion or productivity gains after controlling for broader economic conditions.

key_constraints: Historical growth and productivity estimates use different national-accounting methods and periods; they should not be compared as a single continuous series.

The effects of the Marshall Plan, currency reform and surviving industrial capacity are debated in the economic-history literature; the report presents them as interacting mechanisms, not exclusive causes.
Corporate histories supplied by BMW are relevant primary institutional disclosures but should be read alongside independent Holocaust and occupation-history sources.
The ECB's 0.3% long-run TFP estimate is model-based and is not a guaranteed causal return from any specific defence budget.
The IMF estimates reflect historical European spending episodes and may not transfer directly to the scale and synchronisation of the current defence build-up.

producer_checks.novelty_decision: Long-form historical and institutional analysis; not a daily market brief. Connects war mobilisation to postwar industrial conversion and current defence-spending policy.

revision_reason: Initial long-form research report examining war mobilisation, industrial development and the conversion of defence spending into civilian productive capacity.
revision_scope: Separate wartime mobilisation from physical destruction.
Compare US wartime R&D and postwar conversion with West German reconstruction.
Examine German corporate continuity, forced labour, Allied dismantling and successor structures.
Connect the historical evidence to current ECB and IMF assessments of European defence spending.

en.title: War, Industrial Power and the Limits of the Development Thesis
en.deck: War can accelerate research, industrial coordination and state capacity, but mobilisation is not the same as destruction. The American and German postwar experiences show how surviving capabilities, institutions and external demand determine whether military investment becomes civilian prosperity.
en.regime: Strategic competition and defence mobilisation are again shaping industrial policy, procurement and research priorities across advanced economies.
en.key_risk: Governments may mistake higher defence outlays for durable productive capacity while imports, fragmented procurement and weak civilian spillovers limit domestic learning.

pt-BR.title: Guerra, poder industrial e os limites da tese do desenvolvimento
pt-BR.deck: A guerra pode acelerar pesquisa, coordenação industrial e capacidade estatal, mas mobilização não é o mesmo que destruição. As experiências americana e alemã no pós-guerra mostram como capacidades preservadas, instituições e demanda externa determinam se o investimento militar se converte em prosperidade civil.
pt-BR.regime: A competição estratégica e a mobilização de defesa voltaram a influenciar a política industrial, as compras públicas e as prioridades de pesquisa nas economias avançadas.
pt-BR.key_risk: Governos podem confundir aumento dos gastos de defesa com capacidade produtiva duradoura, enquanto importações, compras fragmentadas e poucos transbordamentos civis limitam o aprendizado doméstico.
